_what_this_is: The test suites known to be RED, so a genuinely new regression can be told from the existing set. Read by tools/known_red_check.py. REPORT ONLY.
_how_it_was_measured: RE-MEASURED 2026-10-06 (fourth). Two passes. (1) tools/run_all_tests.py over the whole tree: 739 files ran, 3 SKIPPED (a precondition, NOT a pass), 84 FAILING. (2) Every failing file not already registered -- 74 of the 84 -- plus the 3 registered files the run showed GREEN, driven INDIVIDUALLY in its own process against a tree checked for drift after every suite. RESULT OF THE INDIVIDUAL DRIVE: 66 RED, 7 GREEN, 4 COULD NOT RUN (300s ceiling). The individual drive is the authority here and the whole-tree run is not, for the reasons in the next field.
_what_an_empty_why_means: NOT DIAGNOSED YET, recorded as empty rather than guessed. An invented cause is worse than a blank one because it ends the investigation. tools/known_red_check.py reports how many entries are undiagnosed, so a blank is a backlog rather than a shrug.
_what_this_is_NOT: Not an allow-list and not a gate. An entry does not make a failure acceptable -- it makes it ATTRIBUTABLE. An entry whose suite has gone GREEN is reported as RECOVERED and must be deleted: while it stands it swallows the next real failure of that file.
measured_against: EVERY suite in the tree, then every failing one re-driven ALONE. tools/run_all_tests.py drove 739 files (344 JS + 395 PY, 3 skipped) and reported 84 FAILING. All 74 of those not already registered were then driven INDIVIDUALLY, one process each, because that whole-tree run is NOT a trustworthy census -- see _why_the_whole_tree_run_was_not_trusted.

entries.tail: This is exit 2. Nothing was checked, and that is not a pass.
entries.why: COULD NOT RUN, exit 2, and it says so in one sentence: 'COULD NOT TELL: could not find `const ROLES_BY_APP = {...};` in api/_lib/auth.js. TEXTBOOK CONVENTION 8, and the check behaves exactly as convention 8 asks: it refuses rather than reporting clean. THE FIX IS SMALL AND IS NOT MINE TO MAKE BLIND -- the anchor must accept an optional wrapper, and whoever owns the vocabulary check should decide whether to parse `roleSet({...})` or to read the resolved object instead of the literal.
